question: Use properties of determinants to show that if the matrix $A$ has two proportional rows, then $\det(A)=0$. Then, apply this result to $\begin{pmatrix}2 & 3 & 4 \\ 4 & 6 & 8 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{pmatrix}$ and compute its determinant.
explanation:
If two rows of a matrix are proportional, then one row can be written as a constant multiple of another row.
By the properties of determinants, if two rows of a determinant are proportional, the determinant becomes zero.
Here the matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}2 & 3 & 4 \\ 4 & 6 & 8 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{pmatrix}$.
Observe that $R_2 = 2R_1$.
Since two rows are proportional, the determinant must be zero.
Verification by expansion:
$2 \begin{vmatrix}6 & 8 \\ -1 & 0\end{vmatrix} - 3 \begin{vmatrix}4 & 8 \\ 1 & 0\end{vmatrix} + 4\begin{vmatrix}4 & 6 \\ 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}$
$= 2(6\cdot0-(-1)\cdot8) - 3(4\cdot0-1\cdot8) + 4(4\cdot-1-1\cdot6)$
$= 2(8) - 3(-8) + 4(-10)$
$= 16 + 24 - 40$
$= 0$.
Thus the determinant is $0$.

options.B: Since $R_2=2R_1$, two rows are proportional, so the determinant is $2$.
options.C: Since $R_2=2R_1$, two rows are proportional, so the determinant is $0$.
options.D: Since no two rows are proportional, the determinant is $-40$.
